memory_update.text: SPSC should be carried forward as the highest-confidence direct underfollowed candidate for retailer-approved product/order data, EDI, assortment, analytics, and execution workflow integration.

Retail inventory visibility has a physical infrastructure layer: item-level RFID chips/readers/platforms from PI and consumable RFID labels/inlays from AVY can support shelf compliance, replenishment, loss prevention, and omnichannel fulfillment.

ADV is a small-cap speculative-shadow candidate for shelf execution, planogram, merchandising, and in-store data collection, but survival to later Serenity layers depends on proving technology/data leverage and manageable labor intensity.

Several strong product-content-management and retail analytics chokepoint vendors appear private rather than US-listed, including Syndigo, Salsify, NIQ, Circana, and Trax; public-market mapping may need indirect exposure or IPO/M&A monitoring.

node: Retail product data, merchandising execution, planogram, inventory visibility, and shelf-compliance services
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around the retail data/execution chokepoint. The strongest direct fit is SPS Commerce, a US-listed retail trading-partner network with SKU, transaction, EDI, assortment, analytics, and retailer-requirement workflow exposure. Second-order infrastructure suppliers include Impinj and Avery Dennison, which provide item-level RFID identity/visibility components and labels that make inventory accuracy, loss prevention, omnichannel fulfillment, and shelf-level execution more automated. Advantage Solutions is a more speculative underfollowed execution-services candidate: it has direct planogram, merchandising, in-store data collection, and retail execution exposure, but needs verification that technology/data leverage offsets labor intensity.
